items.title: Reserve Bank hikes cash rate to 4.1 per cent in a split decision with banks following suit
items.description: The Reserve Bank has lifted interest rates by 0.25 percentage points as the war in the Middle East sends oil, gas, and petrol prices soaring.

items.title: Avoid sugar hits, economists warn, as rate hike pain rolls out
items.description: Economist are urging the government make brave budget calls as Australian households prepare to sweat through another rate rise.

items.title: 'People are DONE': The online MAGA beef over the Iran war
items.description: A civil war within the MAGA movement is getting more lewd by the day as prominent right-wing figures feud online over the war in Iran.

items.title: Kyle Sandilands considering 'many options' amid doubt over radio future
items.description: Radio broadcaster Kyle Sandilands says he is considering "many options" after being taken off-air for insulting his co-host and friend of almost 30 years Jackie "O" Henderson.

items.title: Tropical cyclone declared off Far North Queensland coast
items.description: The tropical low in the Coral Sea is now officially a cyclone, with the system expected to bring destructive winds and heavy rain when it reaches the coast.

items.title: Live: Iran says 10 foreigners arrested for spying as video of attack on US embassy in Baghdad emerges
items.description: A tanker is struck by an unknown projectile while anchored near the Strait of Hormuz, while Donald Trump scolds allies who he claims "weren't that enthusiastic" about helping the US secure the strait. Follow live.

items.title: Ex Iranian footballer says officials are 'mafia-like' as players go home
items.description: Atefe Moradi knows Iranian regime's playbook well. She played for her home country's national league before moving to Australia, and fears for the safety of the female footballers returning to Iran.

items.title: Practical ways to make your tank of fuel last longer
items.description: From fuel-efficient driving to alternative travel modes, we look at practical ways to combat fuel shortages and price hikes.

items.title: Fuel shortages hit tipping point as WA miner stands down most workers
items.description: Fuel shortages linked to the Middle East war are forcing a WA gold miner to stand down workers, exposing how smaller operators are being squeezed while major miners maintain supply.

items.title: 'We haven't seen anything yet': China's plan to kick foreign oil habit
items.description: China is adopting green energy at a scale hard to imagine for many other countries, with the country's latest five-year plan further signalling its intention to reduce its dependency on foreign oil.

items.title: Banksy's real identity revealed in new investigation
items.description: An in-depth investigation drawing on court files, photos and public records says the world-famous anonymous artist is a Bristol-born man who later adopted a new identity.

items.title: How to watch Matildas vs China in Women's Asian Cup semifinal
items.description: The Matildas are in the final four at the Women's Asian Cup, and take on the defending champion China in the first semifinal tonight. Here's how to follow the game at Perth Stadium.

items.title: Former RAAF pilot charged with murder loses legal costs battle
items.description: Robert John Crawford appealed a decision to refuse his legal costs in a District Court battle against Queensland's police commissioner.

items.title: Masseur with 'sex on his brain' jailed after sexually assaulting 13 women
items.description: A masseur who described himself as a nudist is jailed for 15-and-a-half years for sexually assaulting more than a dozen female clients.

items.title: What is vaginismus and how do you know if you have it?
items.description: Madeleine Edwards had never heard of the term vaginismus before she was diagnosed with the condition.

items.title: Why — and how — I'm taking a break from my husband
items.description: After almost five decades of marriage, I needed a break. And since enjoying my new-found freedom, I'm not sure I'll ever go back.

items.title: 'We have exciting days ahead': Danish royals arrive in Melbourne
items.description: The king and queen of Denmark will arrive in Melbourne for the first of two days of royal engagements as part of their Australian state visit.

items.title: Summer swung between extremes as climate change overtook natural drivers
items.description: Scientists warn sharp swings from extreme heat to flooding rain experienced over summer are a sign climate change is overtaking other weather drivers.

items.title: Remote NT town's only major supermarket set to leave region
items.description: Woolworths has run the main supermarket in the NT town of Nhulunbuy since 1972, but is now planning to pull the pin on its operations.

items.title: Bondi gunman's family living in fear, court told
items.description: A lawyer has revealed Naveed Akram's mother and siblings have been targeted with abusive messages, death threats, stalking and pork chops being thrown into their driveway.

items.title: 'You look familiar': When Sasha found a photo of her sister online, she felt 'sick'
items.description: When Sasha Szafranski matched with a stranger on a genealogy website, she uncovered an IVF mix-up that had been hidden for 30 years.

items.title: Navigation sounders turned off before ship hit sea floor, report notes
items.description: A preliminary report has revealed new details about how an Australian research vessel hit the ocean floor after navigational echo sounders were turned off to stop interference with scientific sampling.

items.title: Man, 59, jailed for Molotov cocktail attack on his former high school
items.description: A court hears a 59-year-old man who firebombed a South Coast high school with Molotov cocktails claimed to have been sexually abused by two teachers.

items.title: 'Bakers, mechanics': Ukraine civilians trained by Aussies for Russia war
items.description: Rather than depicting the front line, the Australian War Memorial's new exhibition focuses on preparation for war, the people caught in between and the Australians assisting them.

items.title: US becoming dominant military force in Northern Territory, report says
items.description: Defence analysts have criticised planning around the Northern Territory's defence infrastructure, saying Australia risks becoming the secondary user of the NT's geographic advantages, behind the US military.
